In tools/lint_bank.py, keep the last-number trigger but add one exemption to last_number_disagrees(), after the existing isclose return. Pass when any number in the concluding clause equals the answer. The clause is the text after the last so/thus/therefore/hence/giving. Skip the exemption when the stem asks to combine values, where a listed root can equal the sum by coincidence. Add these next to FINAL_TAIL:

COMBINE_ASK = re.compile(r"\b(?:sum|product|difference)\b|\bhow much (?:greater|less|more)\b|\bvalue of \w+ ?[+−-] ?\w+", re.I)
And add this in last_number_disagrees() before the final return:
    if not COMBINE_ASK.search(item.stem):
        clause = item.rationale[list(CLAUSE_START.finditer(item.rationale))[-1].end():]
        if any(math.isclose(v, expected, rel_tol=1e-5, abs_tol=1e-5) for v in (numeral(m.group().strip()) for m in NUMBER.finditer(clause)) if v is not None):

I ran a patched copy (scratchpad/rfnm/lint_new.py; tools/ untouched). The check drops from 390 to exactly the 132 real findings above, the 8 false-positive templates go to 0, and every other check's rows are byte-identical (total 1969 to 1711). The COMBINE_ASK guard matters: without it, 5 real seeds would be hidden by coincidence (square_equation 12, divide_remainder 13/22/33, and one more). 'how many fewer' is left out of the guard on purpose, or slope_scaled would flag again.
The opposite gap: the CONCLUSION/FINAL_TAIL gating hides real flaws of the same kind. le2.substitute has 46 seeds whose rationale never states the answer, and the check catches 4. A separate check, rationale_omits_answer (the answer value appears nowhere among the rationale's numbers, % scaled, with no tail or conclusion gating), finds 1,206 addresses across 44 templates. Many look like a deliberate house style of stopping one step before the last arithmetic, e.g. tvdata.residual ('the line predicts about 12.0 there'). Adding it is a policy call, so I did not fold it into this check.
